newsitem.title: YEMEN: Initial Yemen poll results give ruling party lead.
newsitem.headline: Initial Yemen poll results give ruling party lead.

text.p: Yemen's ruling General Peoples Congress won 93 constituencies out 126 counted so far and the Islamist Islah party won 16 in the country's first general poll since a 1994 civil war, an election official said on Tuesday.

As of 4.00 p.m. (1300 GMT), results showed independents had won 24 parliamentary seats while other parties won two in Sunday's election, Saeed al-Hekaimi, spokesman for the Supreme Election Committee, told reporters.
Hekaimi did not explain the discrepancy in numbers.

Western diplomats have said the ruling party of President Ali Abdullah Saleh is expected to emerge with a large majority while the Islah, its junior coalition partner, could lose ground. The parliament has 301 seats.

They said independents appeared poised to make strong gains in the ballot, which was overshadowed by shootings in which nine died and allegations of irregularities. Full results are expected by Thursday.

In united Yemen's first elections in 1993, the General Peoples Congress won 123 seats in parliament followed by Islah with 62 and the Yemen Socialist Party with 56. Independents won 47 seats while the rest went to Baathist and Nasserite parties.
